clue.text: Dangerous contraption if Chinamen learn to make it

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are used as raw material to make something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A warning that a risky device can be assembled from simple ingredients by learners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make it' tells you to build the answer from IF, CHINAMEN and LEARN, fifteen letters rearranged into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb or booby trap was traditionally called by this phrase, a hellish device.

clue.text: Listener poorly placed in Eire

indicators.note: letters placed badly are put out of order, so the word listener is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tuning in finds reception bad when sitting somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly placed' signals a rearrangement of LISTENER; the remaining words 'in Eire' point to a region found there.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, containing Dublin.

clue.text: See 1
Martin out, and where to find him

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the name Martin is rearranged

explanation.surface: Martin has gone out, and you are told where he can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals a rearrangement of MARTIN; 'him' refers back to Martin, so the definition plays on the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A county in Northern Ireland is a place where someone could be found.

clue.text: Grinding occupation of a middle — distance athlete about fifty

definitions.note: the definition names a trade by the person who practises it, a grinder of corn

indicators.note: the runner's word goes about, around, the Roman numeral for fifty

parts.note: a miler runs the mile, a classic middle-distance race
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A runner is described as doing a grinding job, around fifty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs a mill grinds grain into flour, so his work is grinding.

clue.text: Information about brushwork familiar to the Dutch school, for example

definitions.text: familiar to the Dutch school, for example

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
brushwork is the art of applying paint

explanation.surface: A remark on painting technique that seventeenth-century Dutch artists knew well.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenes of everyday domestic life were a speciality of the Dutch Golden Age artists.

clue.text: State in which one gets star treatment

definitions.text: State in which one gets star treatment

parts.words: State in which one gets star treatment
parts.note: the condition of being made glamorous, treated like a film star

explanation.surface: A description of a celebrity being pampered.
explanation.definitionFit: Making someone appear glamorous, like a celebrity, is the process described.

clue.text: From which a lot of cackling may be expected

definitions.text: From which a lot of cackling may be expected

parts.words: From which a lot of cackling may be expected
parts.note: cackling is the noise of farm birds, and a lot of it comes from a crowd of them; it also suggests a chattering group of people

explanation.surface: A remark about a noisy group of gossips.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for a flock of honking farmyard birds on the ground.

clue.text: Material to gratify fully around Tyneside

parts.note: to sate is to satisfy completely

indicators.note: around signals turning the region's abbreviation round, back to front

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A fabric chosen to satisfy customers in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the abbreviation for the North East, the region where Tyneside lies, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy cotton fabric woven like satin.

clue.text: Science demanding overtime work

parts.note: overtime work read as work over time, the study of clocks and timekeeping

explanation.surface: A scientific field that needs staff to work extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overtime' suggests extra hours, but read as work 'over time' it is the study and making of timepieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of measuring time and of making clocks and watches.

clue.text: Travel in slipshod gear

definitions.meaning: to move over snow on runners
read as gear one is shod with for slipping along

explanation.surface: Someone travelling in sloppy kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipshod' normally means careless; here it means shod for slipping, a runner worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide across snow, or one of the long runners strapped to boots for it.

clue.text: Sweet-sounding instrument

definitions.meaning: an ice-cream cone is a sweet treat
a brass instrument that makes a sound

explanation.surface: A musical instrument with a lovely tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet-sounding' reads as one adjective, but split it: an ice-cream cone, and a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a wafer cone for ice cream and a small valved brass instrument like a trumpet.

clue.text: They figure symbolically for the count

definitions.text: They figure symbolically for the count

parts.words: They figure symbolically for the count
parts.note: symbols that stand for figures, used in counting

explanation.surface: Characters who play a symbolic role for a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the count' sounds like a nobleman, but it is counting; the symbols that represent figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Written symbols such as 1, 2 and 3 used to denote numbers.

clue.text: Conceit for example, nothing more

indicators.note: more means the next piece is added on after the first

parts.note: O is the zero for nothing

explanation.surface: Vanity, for instance, and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of self-importance, as in an inflated self-image.

clue.text: Standing form of punishment to hold up to ridicule

definitions.meaning: a wooden frame where offenders stood with head and hands locked
to expose someone to public scorn

explanation.surface: A punishment devised to mock offenders publicly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the old stocks-like frame for public shaming and the act of attacking someone publicly with scorn.

clue.text: Little foreign money in aggregate

definitions.meaning: a small coin of Denmark, Norway or Sweden, a hundredth of a krone
rock that is a mixture of minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: A small sum of foreign cash, taken all together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in aggregate' reads as 'in total', but 'in' is a link and the aggregate is mineral-bearing rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a small Scandinavian coin and a naturally occurring rock from which metal is extracted.

clue.text: Feeling experienced first to a formal proposal

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of experienced

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put formally to a meeting

explanation.surface: Someone experiences strong feelings the first time they are formally proposed to.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Something to remind one in passing

definitions.text: Something to remind one in passing

parts.words: Something to remind one in passing
parts.note: a monument that reminds people of someone who has passed away, seen as one passes by

explanation.surface: A note or reminder made casually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in passing' sounds like 'casually', but it refers to death, passing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument or statue erected to commemorate the dead.

clue.text: Deceive as George Washington couldn't

definitions.meaning: the legend of the cherry tree has the young Washington confess, saying he cannot be untruthful

explanation.surface: A remark on lying and the famously honest American president.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak an untruth, which the cherry-tree story says the boy Washington could not do.

clue.text: Mickey-taking slinky creatures?

parts.note: Mickey is the cartoon mouse, so creatures taking mice are cats that hunt them

explanation.surface: Sly animals that tease people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mickey-taking' is British slang for teasing, but here it means taking Mickey Mouse: catching mice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats valued for catching rodents.

clue.text: Former tower of strength on the coast

definitions.text: Former tower of strength on the coast

parts.words: Former tower of strength on the coast
parts.note: a tower of strength usually means a dependable person; here a literal fortified tower on the shore

explanation.surface: A once dependable person living by the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: These are small round coastal forts built in Britain against Napoleonic invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Round defensive forts built along British coasts in the Napoleonic era.

clue.text: It twice upset an Italian master

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the doubled word is read upwards
twice means the word it is written out two times

explanation.surface: Something knocks over an Old Master painting twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles the word It, and 'upset' turns the whole doubled run upside down, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A great Venetian Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Unusual lace to find

indicators.note: unusual letters are out of their normal order, so lace and to are rearranged

explanation.surface: Uncommon lacework that is hard to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges LACE and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover where something is.

clue.text: Andalusian port wine

definitions.meaning: a sweet fortified dessert wine from that region

explanation.surface: A fortified wine from southern Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port wine' reads as one thing, but split: a Spanish port, and a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on Spain's Costa del Sol and the sweet fortified wine named after it.

clue.text: Turn to the Foreign Office initially for its identification?

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for a turn

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone appeals to the Foreign Office to identify something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the fact that the object is by name unidentified.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying object no one can name, so its identity is the very question.

clue.text: Can stitch skirt initially but wouldn't use these for pins

parts.note: a tin is a can
to tack is to stitch loosely

indicators.note: initially asks for just the opening letter of skirt

explanation.surface: Dressmaking advice about tacking a skirt but not pinning it.
explanation.walkthrough: Small nails could be mistaken for pins, but a dressmaker would not use them so.
explanation.definitionFit: Short tinned-iron nails, quite different from the pins a dressmaker uses.

clue.text: Went off, finding me in the way

indicators.note: in means the small word sits inside the word for the way

parts.note: a road is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone left, finding themselves an obstruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the way' looks like 'obstructing', but 'in' is the container signal and 'the way' is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wandered off without a fixed route.

clue.text: Hobson's choice, as it were

parts.note: a Cambridge stable-keeper offered customers only the horse nearest the door: take it or leave it

explanation.surface: A remark about a choice that is no choice at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobson's choice comes from a Cambridge livery-stable owner who made customers take the horse nearest the door or none.
explanation.definitionFit: Only one option is available, so there is nothing else to pick.
